issues.title: Control panel for Core Mapping
issues.body:
We require some general controls for the Core Mapping channel.

Here is a mockup:
https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1LdTKv9BTrJdnfshJeEz6SpmMML8D_kbNc8emZ-Ugw6Q/edit#slide=id.g29d5206fb52_0_40

(more detail on following slide)

The aim here is for them not to be focussed on a particular wargame, style of data, or set of properties [*].  So, the UI will largely be build using retrospection from the current features on the map

* [x] create left-hand control panel. It's width (as a %age, I guess) should be persistent
* [x] create top `Filters` panel.  It should have a `filters` heading.  It should start with zero filters, but should have an `add` button to add a new filter.   The `add` button will popup a list of known properties (I don't yet know where these will come from. Either by doing a "live" scan of current data, or on each new update to `features`
* [x] create central `Items` panel. This will be a list of the currently visible items.  For `MilSymbol` it will show the symbol, for `CoreRenderer` item it will be a generic `shape` icon, shaded using the `color` for that item
* [x] create lower `properties` panel.   If one item is selected in the `items` listing, show it's properties here.  We're display text-boxes or drop-downs depending on what we can determine from the property.  We won't show properties with a leading underscore.


[*] - ok, we'll allow a _few_ predictable properties. `sidc` for MilSymbols and `color` for all features.

- The list of items will be changed based on the results of the filter value
- Clicking on add button opens a popup/modal, it shows all the properties of the current data (just for now), but when we select a property and add, what should it do next according to?

Hello @lebaphi  - I tried to mock up the filter component here:
https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1LdTKv9BTrJdnfshJeEz6SpmMML8D_kbNc8emZ-Ugw6Q/edit#slide=id.g29d5206fb52_0_64

When we select a property and add it, a new filter will be shown in the table.  It will have a text box or a drop-down list.  Initially, the text-box will be empty, or the drop-down list will have zero items selected.  That means that filter is currently inactive, and is ignored.  If the user enters some text, or selects an item from the drop-down, that filter becomes active, and we start filtering items accordingly (applying wildcard search if it's a text box)
